decisions.executionNote: Begin a symmetric, elbow-up approach to the two ends of the straightedge, gradually turning the open grippers downward.
Continue turning both open grippers toward an overhead pinch, staying above the ruler and outside the blocks.
Continue the gradual overhead approach with both arms remaining on their own sides.
Keep rotating smoothly toward vertical fingers while advancing to the ends of the ruler.
Finish most of the wrist reorientation above the tool; maintain symmetric separated arm configurations.
Move above the ruler ends and nearly complete vertical orientation before lowering; tool contact height remains uncertain.
Square the grippers to the ruler and lower slightly at points inset from its ends; assess clearance before closing.
Lower the open grippers slowly toward the ruler while keeping the tool flat and the cubes untouched.
Reduce the jaw span while descending gently, to localize the ruler between the fingers without lifting anything.
Relieve slight table contact and close on the ruler at both ends, keeping it at tabletop height.
Test a slow level slide toward the blocks with both jaws closed; verify that the ruler follows without lifting cubes.
Slide the ruler forward at constant low height to collect the nearest cube against its straight edge.
Continue the level sweep so all three cubes contact the same edge and rotate into parallel faces; no upward motion.
Advance a short additional distance to straighten the remaining skewed middle cube against the ruler.
The three visible front faces now form a straight parallel row. Withdraw the ruler a short distance along the table before releasing and resetting.
Release the straightedge onto the table away from the aligned cubes, then begin lifting only the empty hands.
Retract and raise the empty grippers clear of the released ruler, preserving the visibly aligned row and elbow-up continuity.
Return along a smooth separated-arm path, gradually restoring the original wrist orientations while leaving the ruler and cubes stationary.
Continue restoring the home pose with empty open grippers, maintaining the reverse elbow-up path.
Continue the controlled homeward retreat, with no contact with the aligned row or released ruler.
Bring both wrists back toward their initial positions and yaw while the completed-looking row remains undisturbed.
Continue the final portion of the homeward path, keeping both grippers open and clear of the objects.
Slow the final approach to the recorded home poses to maintain joint continuity and avoid an abrupt reset.
